policies.score: Score each item independently: 0 demonstrated material defect; 1 evidenced partial satisfaction; 2 item acceptance conditions met; 3 stated robustness beyond 2. No overall or parent aggregate. An unrun, blocked or insufficiently evidenced item is NOT_ASSESSED, not 0. NOT_APPLICABLE requires a scope-specific reason.
policies.measurements: Record raw measures and their units, denominators, missingness and uncertainty alongside the ordinal score. Set any risk/error/coverage targets before qualification; no universal numeric threshold is supplied.
policies.methods: Checks are grouped by the mechanism that produces their evidence. A script calling a model is not a deterministic semantic check. Alternative methods are conditional, not a requirement to execute every stage. A trained decision model or LLM judge needs scope-matched qualification before its output supports a material score.
policies.independence: Human review denotes authority, independent verification or adjudication—not a requirement to manually inspect every case. Preserve reviewer disagreements; dependent pipeline stages are not independent corroboration.
policies.qualification: Assess all applicable items used for the stated claim; unknowns cannot support full qualification. A qualified alternative may replace an unavailable method, with rationale retained. Optional monitors do not block unrelated claims. Agent failure and detected sensitive/unsafe behavior do not themselves make the evaluation invalid.
policies.work_items: Each implementation task names a deliverable, not an existing implemented runner. Completion means the listed checks produce evidence satisfying the acceptance anchor. Implementation tests do not count as live evaluation proof.
policies.reuse: Each item has one definition. Other skills reference it and bind results to their subject/revision. Reuse qualified evidence only while assumptions and identities remain applicable; do not count reuse as independent replication.
policies.ethos: ETHOS records intended behavior, not a summary of current code or existing eval coverage. First-Eval / Create owns CREATE-09 through CREATE-15; Audit reuses them, and Environment consumes the applicable scope/tool/failure contracts. File-only Discover does not require an ETHOS review. Reuse valid confirmation and qualification until material identity, intent, content or evidence changes. Explicit unknowns remain visible; do not invent intent, targets or permission.

items.title: Task artifact access
items.question: Can the authorized reviewer read the task instructions and required input artifacts?
items.requirement: Discover inventories an existing task or suite.
items.scope: Task definition at an identified revision.
items.measurement: Required task artifacts are listed as accessible, missing, denied or unresolved; count each status against the declared inventory.

checks.action: Read manifests and explicit references to inventory task instructions, input fixtures and task metadata.
checks.expected_evidence: Inventory with artifact role and reference origin.

checks.action: Resolve each location using reviewer permissions; record readability and revision or digest without exposing secrets.
Independently verify the task-artifact inventory against the selected source.

scoring.0: A confirmed missing or denied required task artifact prevents material inspection.
scoring.1: Some required task artifacts are readable, but known inventory or identity gaps remain.
scoring.2: Every declared required task artifact is accessible and identified; no material task-input reference remains unresolved.
scoring.3: An independent review verifies the same inventory and access results without undocumented information.

items.on_gap: Request the exact missing artifact or permission; limit claims to inspected material.
items.boundary: Does not establish scorer correctness, execution readiness or solver permissions. An incomplete search cannot prove no artifacts exist.
items.implementation_task: Build a manifest/reference inventory checker that emits per-artifact access and identity records.

items.title: Grading-path identification
items.question: Can the reviewer determine which scorer and scoring configuration apply to this task?
items.requirement: A discovered evaluation assigns a score or verdict.
items.scope: Task-to-scorer selection at the selected configuration.
items.measurement: Each task maps to a scorer entry point and scoring configuration; unresolved or ambiguous selections are listed, not guessed.

checks.action: Resolve scorer registrations, entry points and configured dispatch rules; retain task-to-scorer links.
checks.expected_evidence: Selection map with supporting configuration references.

checks.action: Use existing run metadata to compare the selected scorer with the declared route.
checks.when: Matching run metadata is already available; do not launch a run for inventory alone.

checks.action: Inspect code when configuration cannot resolve selection; document dynamic rules or the unresolved boundary.
Propose an interpretation of an ambiguous dispatch rule using exact code/configuration evidence.
checks.when: Optional assistance only; it cannot establish behavior of inaccessible code.

checks.action: Independently resolve the same grading path from the recorded packet.

scoring.0: Evidence confirms the inventory names the wrong scorer or omits a material active grading branch.
scoring.1: A scorer is identified, but a known dispatch or configuration ambiguity remains.
scoring.2: The selected scorer, configuration and applicable selection rules are identified with no unresolved material branch.
scoring.3: An independent reviewer resolves the same selection without undocumented information.

evidence: Dynamic selection rules and unresolved cases
items.on_gap: Obtain the dispatch configuration or code; label opaque remote selection unresolved.
items.boundary: Identify the grading route, not whether it grades correctly. Dynamic selection does not automatically require a model or execution.
items.implementation_task: Build a scorer-selection resolver and an unresolved-dispatch report.

items.title: Grading dependency access
items.question: Can the reviewer access the artifacts needed to inspect the selected grading path?
items.requirement: A grading path has been identified or its known branches are being inventoried.
items.scope: Scorer dependencies for the selected task/configuration.
items.measurement: Inventory tests, expected results, datasets, judge prompts and rubrics by reference; report accessible/missing/denied/unresolved counts.

checks.action: Follow declared scorer references to tests, reference answers, datasets, judge prompts, rubrics and configuration.
Check reviewer access and record versions/digests for each material dependency; mark external or unresolved artifacts.
Inspect unclear imports, generated references or external-service contracts for undeclared dependencies.
checks.expected_evidence: Additional dependency evidence or explicit inspection limit.
checks.when: Declared references do not settle completeness.

checks.action: Independently verify dependency coverage and access against the selected scorer.

scoring.0: A confirmed missing or inaccessible material grading dependency prevents inspection.
scoring.1: Known grading dependencies are partly accessible, but material coverage or identity gaps remain.
scoring.2: All identified material dependencies are accessible and version-bound; review leaves no unresolved material dependency.
scoring.3: Independent review verifies dependency coverage and access without undocumented information.

items.on_gap: Request missing review material; do not infer inaccessible grading behavior.
items.boundary: Reviewer access does not authorize exposing artifacts to the solver. Test solver information boundaries separately under Audit/Environment/Create; do not claim leakage resistance here.
items.implementation_task: Build a dependency walker with access/version checks and a queue for unresolved references.

items.title: Declared configuration identity
items.question: Is the evaluated agent and its declared configuration identifiable?
items.requirement: Discovery describes an agent/application or interprets its evaluation setup.
items.measurement: Required configuration fields have values and sources, or explicit provider-unavailable status; no guessed identities.

checks.action: Record agent/application/model identity, prompts, sampling, budgets, harness, permissions and dependency identities from authorized configuration.
Mark omitted, inaccessible and provider-hidden fields separately; validate required fields and version references.
Assess which unknown settings limit the stated interpretation or comparison.
Independently reconstruct the declared manifest from its sources.
checks.when: For level 3; reconstruct configuration records, not the agent or grader.

scoring.0: A confirmed material identity omission or misstatement makes the claimed setup uninterpretable.
scoring.1: The configuration is partly identified, with known material source or version gaps.
scoring.2: All obtainable relevant settings are sourced; provider-hidden settings and their claim limits are explicit.
scoring.3: Independent source review reproduces the manifest and its limitations.

items.on_gap: Resolve missing identities or narrow the supported claim.
items.boundary: This records declared settings; observed run agreement is assessed separately. No credentials or unavailable provider internals are inferred.
items.implementation_task: Build a configuration manifest extractor with explicit unknown-state validation.

items.title: Observed configuration agreement
items.question: Did the run use the configuration being reported?
items.requirement: A result or readiness claim relies on an existing or authorized run.
items.scope: Run bound to task and configuration revision.
items.measurement: Compare obtainable observed settings against declared settings; report matched, mismatched and unobservable fields.

checks.action: Bind run metadata to task/configuration identities and compare model, prompt, limits, harness, tools and dependency settings.
checks.expected_evidence: Per-field declared/observed diff and run binding.

checks.action: Keep unavailable observed settings as unknown rather than treating them as matching.
Repeat with the recorded configuration and verify expected configuration/control observations.
checks.expected_evidence: Independent repeat metadata and control receipts.
checks.when: For level 3, only with execution authorization.

scoring.0: A material declared/observed mismatch invalidates the reported setup or comparison.
scoring.1: Observed configuration is partly checked, with known material mismatches or observability gaps unresolved.
scoring.2: All obtainable material settings agree or justified differences bound the claim; unknown internals remain explicit.
scoring.3: An authorized independent repeat reproduces configuration and expected control observations.

items.on_gap: Correct configuration attribution or narrow claims; do not silently transfer scores between configurations.
items.boundary: No run means NOT_ASSESSED, not an instruction to execute. Matching settings alone does not prove correct grading.
items.implementation_task: Build a declared-versus-observed configuration comparator keyed by run/task revision.

items.title: Runtime route compatibility
items.question: Does the task manifest match the selected runtime route?
items.requirement: Runtime readiness, not file-only inventory, is requested.
items.scope: Selected Gym, Harbor or agreed alternative and task manifest.
items.measurement: Provider-owned manifest validation and adapter compatibility results, including errors and skipped checks.

checks.action: Identify the agreed provider, runtime/adapter version and task manifest; run authorized provider validation.
Distinguish missing runtime, unsupported manifest and validation failure from agent behavior.
Validate known-invalid manifests and a clean supported configuration.
checks.when: For level 3, within authorized runtime checks.

scoring.0: Provider validation confirms a material incompatibility with the declared route.
scoring.1: The route is identified but known manifest or adapter gaps remain.
scoring.2: The selected provider validates the manifest and required adapter compatibility.
scoring.3: Independent clean setup and invalid-manifest controls confirm correct compatibility detection.

items.on_gap: Resolve the manifest/adapter mismatch before claiming compatible readiness.
items.boundary: Compatibility is not an end-to-end smoke pass. File-only Discover leaves this unassessed.
items.implementation_task: Wrap provider validation into a typed compatibility receipt without running the target agent.

items.title: Comparison setup fairness
items.question: Are material setup differences justified for the comparison being claimed?
items.requirement: When comparing systems, disclose prompts, tools, budgets, scaffolds, scorer settings and model-specific accommodations.
items.scope: task; When comparing systems, disclose prompts, tools, budgets, scaffolds, scorer settings and model-specific accommodations.
items.measurement: Count and classify material configuration differences; adjudicate each justification and measure paired outcome/decision sensitivity to disputed differences.

checks.action: Diff prompts, tool permissions, budgets, scaffolds and scoring configuration across systems.
checks.when: During assessment of the declared revision

checks.action: Decide whether each material difference or model-specific accommodation is justified by the intended comparison.
checks.when: During assessment of the declared revision

checks.action: Run matched configuration comparisons for differences whose effect remains disputed.
checks.expected_evidence: Paired results at fixed task/system identities
checks.when: When a material fairness dispute requires authorized testing

scoring.1: Known differences lack adequate justification or testing
scoring.2: Differences disclosed and justified for intended comparison
scoring.3: Matched sensitivity tests support conclusions across plausible setups

items.on_gap: Correct unjustified advantages or limit the comparative claim
items.boundary: Assess setup fairness, not biased trace content. Identical configurations are not universally required. Missing or unrun evidence is NOT_ASSESSED, not 0; justified exclusions are NOT_APPLICABLE. Referenced code is supporting material, not verified runnable integration. Execute interventions only with approval; qualify any material judge/classifier and routing dependency before using its verdict.
items.implementation_task: Build a comparative setup review packet with matched sensitivity experiments for disputed accommodations.

items.title: Verify solver tool access
items.question: Can the solver exercise every required tool contract under its actual permissions?
items.requirement: When task completion depends on tools or permissioned actions.
items.measurement: Required actions with usable solver-visible tool contracts / all required actions; passing schema/call/reset/error probes / applicable probes.

checks.action: Map required task actions to solver-visible tools and required permission boundaries.
Compare exposed schemas and permission/configuration snapshots with the required tool contract.
Exercise supported calls, reset and expected errors under solver permissions within the authorized side-effect boundary.
checks.expected_evidence: Actual solver-identity preflight and error/reset receipts.

scoring.0: A required action is demonstrably inaccessible or wrong under solver permissions.
scoring.1: Some required tool contracts work with demonstrated partial coverage.
scoring.2: Every required tool and permission contract passes applicable probes.
scoring.3: Clean-runtime reset, error and boundary probes independently corroborate access.

evidence: Actual solver-identity preflight and error/reset receipts.
items.on_gap: Provision required tools or obtain an explicit scope change. Unknown or not run: NOT_ASSESSED, not a defect; justified inapplicability: NOT_APPLICABLE.
items.boundary: Do not grant extra permissions or silently omit required capabilities; readiness must be independent of task reward.
items.implementation_task: Deliver an action/tool coverage map and solver-permission preflight packet.

items.title: Inventory dependencies and substitution approval
items.question: Is every required component available in an explicitly authorized form?
items.requirement: When a task depends on software, tools, MCP endpoints or replacements.
items.measurement: Available real or scope-owner-approved components / all required components; revision-matched approvals / substitutions.

checks.action: Inventory each required component and MCP endpoint as real, approved mock/replay, missing or unknown, with observed identity.
Obtain scope-owner approval for each substitution, naming allowed differences and revision.
checks.expected_evidence: Scoped owner approval; absence is not implied consent.

checks.action: Match installed substitution identities and declared differences to approval records.

scoring.0: A required component is confirmed missing or an active substitution is unapproved.
scoring.1: Inventory and authorizations are evidenced but only partially reconciled.
scoring.2: Every required component is available as real or explicitly approved replacement.
scoring.3: Independent provisioning/approval reconciliation corroborates the inventory.

evidence: Scoped owner approval; absence is not implied consent.
items.on_gap: Provision real dependencies or obtain approval before substitution. Unknown or not run: NOT_ASSESSED, not a defect; justified inapplicability: NOT_APPLICABLE.
items.boundary: Approval is not fidelity evidence; ENV-02-B independently assesses behavior. Unknown availability is NOT_ASSESSED.
items.implementation_task: Deliver a dependency bill of materials and revision-bound substitution approvals.

items.title: Control external state
items.question: Are pinned and intentionally live dependencies bounded well enough to interpret outcomes?
items.requirement: When time, web/API responses, mutable data, packages, images or remote services influence the task.
items.measurement: Captured/pinned or explicitly bounded live dependencies / material external dependencies; interpreted outcomes under declared drift controls.

checks.action: Inventory material dependencies; record pins/snapshots or live time, source and response identities.
checks.expected_evidence: Dependency manifest and retained snapshot/response references.

checks.action: Define acceptable live-state drift and the outcome relation expected under relevant changes.
Replay or deliberately perturb relevant state and compare behavior/state and grading against the declared relation.
checks.expected_evidence: Revision-bound replay/drift outcomes and unresolved attribution.

scoring.0: Observed drift materially invalidates expected outcomes or comparisons.
scoring.1: Some state is captured with evidenced remaining capture/pinning gaps.
scoring.2: All material dependencies are controlled or live limits and observations support the bounded claim.
scoring.3: Independent replay and deliberate drift tests corroborate interpretation.

evidence: Dependency manifest and retained snapshot/response references.
Revision-bound replay/drift outcomes and unresolved attribution.
items.on_gap: Freeze material state, repair grading for permitted variation, or narrow reproducibility claims. Unknown or not run: NOT_ASSESSED, not a defect; justified inapplicability: NOT_APPLICABLE.
items.boundary: Permitted state variation need not preserve reward when correct task outcomes change; distinguish grader and behavior effects.
items.implementation_task: Deliver an external-state manifest with live drift bounds and replay-control results.

items.title: Evidence revision consistency
items.question: Are results bound to compatible identities and invalidated when material dependencies change?
items.requirement: For every task result or reused qualification packet, bind all material instruction, data, scoring and runtime identities.
items.scope: task; For every task result or reused qualification packet, bind all material instruction, data, scoring and runtime identities.
items.measurement: Results with complete compatible identity links / results reviewed; stale affected results after each material change; preserved regrading lineage. Change-injection tests measure invalidation coverage.

checks.action: Bind instructions, fixtures, scorer, ground truth, judge prompt/configuration and material runtime/dependency identities to each result.
checks.when: During assessment of the declared revision

checks.action: Compare current and evidence identities; invalidate affected scores on material changes and retain original results plus regrading history.
checks.when: During assessment of the declared revision

checks.action: Test declared identity-change fixtures to confirm affected evidence invalidates while unchanged evidence lineage remains intact.
checks.when: When verifying robustness of evidence reuse

checks.action: Bind ETHOS revision and obligation references to task and qualification evidence; use declared change-impact mappings to invalidate affected assumptions after ETHOS changes. Test changed-content and unchanged-reuse fixtures.
checks.expected_evidence: ETHOS change-impact and stale-evidence report; fixture outcomes.
checks.when: When task meaning or qualification depends on ETHOS; unresolved semantic change impact requires authorized review, not an inferred unchanged status.

scoring.1: Version metadata incomplete or stale reviews remain
scoring.2: All material changes tracked and evidence bound
scoring.3: Change-injection tests invalidate stale results and preserve lineage

evidence: ETHOS change-impact and stale-evidence report; fixture outcomes.
items.on_gap: Rerun affected checks before transferring prior scores to a changed evaluation
items.boundary: Reuse only matching configuration, semantics, channels, permissions and population support; matching hashes do not establish holdout independence. Rerun only affected checks, but do not transfer stale scores. Missing or unrun evidence is NOT_ASSESSED, not 0; justified exclusions are NOT_APPLICABLE. Referenced code is supporting material, not verified runnable integration. Execute interventions only with approval; qualify any material judge/classifier and routing dependency before using its verdict.
items.implementation_task: Build a result identity manifest and scoped evidence-invalidation report with change fixtures.
